      <title>Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after suspected Ukrainian drone attack</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya</link>
      <description><p>No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia</p><p>A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.</p><p>The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state</link>
      <description><p>Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded</p><p>Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.</p><p>Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/19/baobab-five-trees-south-africa-dug-up-export-blocked-georgia-aoe</link>
      <description><p>The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits</p><p>Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.</p><p>The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover.       <description><p>Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds</p><p>One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.</p><p>In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament.       <description><p>New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Company helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people</p><p>• <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/ng-interactive/2026/sep/16/slave-trade-wealth-britain-financial-system-bank-of-england-enslaved-africans">Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds</a></p><p>British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.</p><p>Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/22/bank-of-england-directors-illegally-profited-enslavement-cuba">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Foreign combatants in Port-au-Prince welcomed by many after years of gang control but some fear offensive could exacerbate volatile situation</p><p>A bullet-peppered mural of the Haitian striker Emmanuel Sanon covers the facade of Port-au-Prince’s main football ground. But more than two years have passed since any sports stars graced the pitch.</p><p>In 2024, as the surrounding city was <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/audio/2024/nov/19/inside-port-au-prince-haiti-the-capital-where-gangs-have-taken-over-podcast">almost entirely captured by heavily armed gangs</a>, Sylvio Cator stadium – where football greats including Brazil’s Ronaldo and Roberto Carlos once played – also fell under criminal control, its dilapidated red and blue stands used as an outpost by fighters working for a gang boss called Izo. Haiti’s national team, the Grenadiers, found itself homeless and was <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/13/we-can-do-much-how-feeling-for-family-helped-end-haitis-long-world-cup-absence">forced to play its World Cup qualifying games abroad</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/21/excitement-unease-haiti-el-salvador-troops-gangs-war-bukele">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>President says Kyiv responsible for sinking Merkury warship in Benghazi on Sunday and also drone attack on cargo vessel MV Angara</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after suspected Ukrainian drone attack</a></p></li></ul><p><strong>Turning to Ukraine, Nato’s Rutte stresses the need to secure the flow of “crucial supplies” or air defence weapons and ammunition to Ukraine.</strong></p><p><em><strong>“</strong>It helps Ukraine to defend itself today, but it also strengthens Ukraine’s hands in any future negotiations with Russia. … But support needs to be concrete. <strong>We have to show Putin that his attempts to weaken our support will fail.”</strong></em></p><p><em>“Our citizens need to know that the lights will stay on, that their homes will stay warm, that hospitals, transport and communications will keep working.”</em></p><p><em>“One day it can be in the form of an arson attack against a factory or drones disrupt disrupting an airport. The next, it is sabotaged railways or cargo vessels targeted at sea and cyber-attacks.”</em></p><p><em>“It’s all happening now, and it won’t go away anytime soon. … <strong>The conclusion of all of this is that we are all targeted,</strong> that we are all affected – when it comes to our pipelines, our cables, our energy grids and our economies – and they are all interconnected. … That means that we are all in this for the long term, and <strong>therefore we must step up to the plate, to ensure that, we stay ahead of danger.”</strong></em></p><p><em>“But if we are serious about keeping our alliance strong and secure, then <strong>all allies must pull their weight not only in 2035, but starting now.</strong> At least, everybody needs to have the credible path to get there.”</em></p><p><em>“These investments are also a boon to prosperity.       <title>From mocked to mainstream: how Spain’s far-right Vox transformed its fortunes</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/vox-party-spain-far-right-mocked-to-mainstream</link>
      <description><p>Party that won just 0.2% of the vote in 2016 is on course for almost 20% this time and could be part of next government</p><p>Almost exactly eight years ago, a video clip of a stocky, bearded man riding a horse through western Andalucía <a href="https://www.antena3.com/noticias/espana/santiago-abascal-vox-caballo-reconquistar-andalucia-video_201811135beaadcc0cf200fa81f731e1.html">went viral in Spain</a>. The rider was Santiago Abascal, the leader of the far-right Vox party, the soundtrack was a bombastic snatch of the Lord of the Rings score, and the caption was an equally unsubtle callback to the 700-year fight to wrest the Iberian peninsula from Islamic rule. <em>“La Reconquista comenzará en tierras andaluzas,”</em> it read – the reconquest will begin on Andalucían soil.</p><p>Celebrated by some, jeered by others – and <a href="https://x.com/Proscojoncio/status/1061981999861325824">inventively lampooned</a> by those with sufficient skill and time on their hands – the video didn’t seem quite as amusing three weeks later when Vox <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/dec/09/far-right-andalucia-seville-vox-party-shockwave-spanish-politics">broke through into the political mainstream</a> by winning 12 seats in Andalucía’s regional parliament.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/vox-party-spain-far-right-mocked-to-mainstream">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>Monday briefing: What could Andy Burnham’s reset mean for the UK?</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/monday-briefing-what-could-andy-burnhams-reset-mean-for-the-uk</link>
      <description><p>In today’s newsletter: The prime minister has reopened the debate over a future relationship with a changed EU – as the bloc faces the rise of the far right, a protectionist economic agenda and growing defence ambitions</p><p>Good morning. Nobody really wants to think about Brexit any more, save for the original Brexiters, who seem delighted that Andy Burnham’s “reset” with the EU has given them an excuse to get the old gang back together. But arguments about whether the UK should rejoin the EU will reignite in parliament this week, as Burnham briefs MPs on the deal he agreed on Friday.</p><p>That deal wasn’t so much a victory as the culmination of Keir Starmer’s incrementalist approach to UK-EU relations. Its core agreements haven’t been ratified by member states yet, and the EU won’t sign them off until Britain resolves a dispute over tuition fees for European students. Burnham is apparently “determined” to take the UK back into the EU, but don’t expect any progress on that before the next general election.</p><p><em><strong>Cop</strong></em><em><strong>31 </strong></em>| The EU, the UK and allies in the developing world <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/22/cop31-climate-talks-set-to-end-in-deep-division-as-key-deal-rejected">rejected what they called an unacceptable deal</a> that “failed to meet the moment” in a dramatic finish to the UN talks in Turkey. The proposed deal failed to endorse a away from fossil fuels that more than 130 countries demanded.</p><p><em><strong>Russia </strong></em>| A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in a suspected <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">Ukrainian sea drone attack</a>, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.</p><p><em><strong>Weapons</strong></em>| The Red Cross and other rights groups <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/science/2026/nov/22/red-cross-warns-too-late-regulate-autonomous-weapons-united-nations">have warned that it will soon</a> be too late to properly regulate the development of autonomous weapons. The warning came as the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons concluded without an agreement on an instrument for regulating autonomous weapons.</p><p><em><strong>UK news </strong></em>| Dozens of hospitals are so short of money they may not be able to continue caring for patients and are being forced to make “unpalatable” cuts to services and staff,<a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/22/nhs-savings-hospitals-trusts-england-cuts"> the Guardian can reveal.</a></p><p><em><strong>West Bank </strong></em>| Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/netanyahu-rival-condemns-settler-arson-attacks-palestinian-villages-west-bank">condemned arson attacks</a> by militant Israeli settlers on Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank after dozens of settlers raided Palestinian communities overnight on Saturday.</p><p><em><strong>Monday</strong></em> | FIFA is set to announce that the UK will host the 2035 Women’s World Cup.</p><p><em><strong>Thursday </strong></em>| RMT will begin a series of eight 24-hour strikes on the London Underground over the next three months due to a dispute over a four-day week for its drivers.</p><p><em><strong>Sunday</strong></em> | Spain will hold snap parliamentary elections in what will be the country’s sixth general election in 11 years.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/monday-briefing-what-could-andy-burnhams-reset-mean-for-the-uk">Continue reading...</a></description>

Christian Boltanski, one of France's top contemporary artists whose multimedia works probed the meaning of mortality and memory, has died aged 76, a former museum director told AFP on Sunday.

French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a planned 1.6% increase in the minimum wage would be brought forward from January to December after holding talks with trade unions and business leaders over the cost-of-living crisis that has fuelled weeks of unrest across France. The increase fell well short of the demands of unions, which have called for fresh protests in the coming days.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <description><p>After chaos at airlines, banks and companies from Microsoft to Apple, people have become convinced the world’s systems are under attack</p><p>Nicole Reindorf’s American Airlines flight was ready for takeoff in Phoenix when the pilot came on the intercom and announced what was to become the longest nationwide aviation shutdown since <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/september11">9/11</a>.</p><p>Reindorf, 70, had seen the headlines hours before about a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/live/2026/nov/13/microsoft-outage-down-today-live-update-outlook-teams-365-when-fixed-latest-status-cause-news">global Microsoft outage</a>. She immediately suspected the two were linked in some way by AI-related threats – and that she would not get to the wedding of her best friend’s son in California.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/22/hacks-ai-internet-outages-airlines-banks-microsoft-apple">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Two weeks after Democrats flipped Congress, conservative outlets are having conversations on whether to distance themselves from Trump or double down on Maga</p><p>As a so-called “blue wave” crashed across the country on the night of 3 November, conservative hosts and commentators on Fox News <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/04/trump-blames-fox-news-republican-losses">displayed an almost virtuosic ability to avoid directly blaming Donald Trump</a> for the Republican party’s defeat, instead pinning the blame on impertinent voters who didn’t grasp the strength of the economy.</p><p>“In some sense, Mr Trump was too successful in the first year and didn’t sell it enough in the second year,” said Larry Kudlow, a Fox Business Network host who served as the president’s director of the National Economic Council during his first administration.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/22/conservative-media-trump-midterm-elections-results">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/20/global-stock-markets-slump-anthropic-ipo-ai-sell-off</link>
      <description><p>The Nasdaq lost trillions in value, with the AI startup’s IPO failing to buoy it as investors question huge sums being poured into AI buildout</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/19/who-are-anthropic-founders">Who are Anthropic’s seven co-founders, now worth $180bn?</a></p></li></ul><p>As Anthropic’s stock dropped during its second day of trading, the wider stock market dipped with it. On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite erased all its gains for 2026 and closed down 5% from its value on 1 January.       <title>Labor leaders call on governments to stop awarding Amazon public contracts</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/19/labor-unions-amazon-contracts-open-letter</link>
      <description><p>Union leaders from 19 countries urge reassessment of ties to Amazon, citing company’s poor record on worker rights</p><p>More than 30 labor union leaders from 19 countries are calling on governments to review their public contracts with Amazon and Amazon Web Services, citing the company’s poor record on worker rights and collective bargaining, in an<a href="https://uniglobalunion.org/wp-content/uploads/Amazon-procurement-letter-embargoed-until-nov-19.pdf"> open letter</a> published on Thursday.</p><p>“Amazon’s consistent record of disrespect for workers’ fundamental rights should disqualify it from being awarded public contracts – its behaviour is fundamentally inconsistent with the shared democratic values of our countries,” the union leaders wrote.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/19/labor-unions-amazon-contracts-open-letter">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>UK central bank will want to avoid echoes of expensive US Federal Reserve revamp that led to Trump clash</p><p>Andrew Bailey may spend his days closely watching developments in the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/strait-of-hormuz">strait of Hormuz</a> or US stock markets for signs of shocks to the global economy – but the Bank of England’s governor has a £160m problem brewing much closer to home.</p><p>A secretive major revamp of the Bank’s historic headquarters in the heart of London’s Square Mile presents a huge test of Bailey’s project management skills.       <title>Infantino’s $20bn World Cup sell-off plan was to run for up to 96 years, documents show</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/gianni-infantino-world-cup-sell-off-plan-96-years-documents-payouts</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Management team were in line for huge payouts</p></li><li><p>Fifa denies Infantino would have profited from plan</p></li></ul><p>Gianni Infantino’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/aug/01/fifa-scraps-plan-to-sell-off-stakes-in-world-cup-after-widespread-backlash">failed Fifa Forward Enterprise plan</a> could have locked football in for up to 96 years while paying its management up to 5% of the scheme’s multibillion-pound value, according to documents seen by the Guardian.</p><p>Previously undisclosed communications by Fifa and Thrive Capital, the lead investor for the proposal, cast fresh light on the deal to sell off football’s crown jewels. They outline a plan, produced days before July’s final of the 2026 World Cup, to profit from the sport’s burgeoning commercial revenues for almost a century.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/gianni-infantino-world-cup-sell-off-plan-96-years-documents-payouts">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Inside Fifa and US Soccer’s plan for 2031 World Cup: ‘the largest women’s sporting event in history’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/2031-womens-world-cup-projection-fifa-ussf</link>
      <description><p>The US-led four-country bid will be confirmed in Zurich on Monday, projecting record-setting total revenues of $4bn</p><p>The biggest and most lucrative event in the history of women’s sport will be confirmed at an Extraordinary Fifa Congress in Zurich on Monday, with a joint bid from the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031’s Women’s World Cup to be formally ratified by a vote of Fifa’s 211 member associations.</p><p>In the bid book submitted to Fifa last year the prospective hosts pledged to generate total revenues of $4bn if awarded hosting rights, which would represent a staggering increase on the $570m earnings from the last World Cup held in Australia and New Zealand three years ago, the first women’s tournament to break even.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/2031-womens-world-cup-projection-fifa-ussf">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘Haaland must be worried’: Thierno Barry’s rise has David Moyes purring</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/thierno-barry-rise-david-moyes-purring-everton</link>
      <description><p>Everton striker has worked hard to find his scoring touch after admitting he hit ‘rock bottom’ at times last season</p><p>A most unexpected name sits behind the phenomenon Erling Haaland and the £125m proven marksman Alexander Isak in the Premier League goalscoring chart this season. The rise of Thierno Barry may have surprised even the man himself but stands as a fitting reward for single-minded perseverance and the refusal to quit.</p><p>“Fabulous” was David Moyes’s take on Barry’s last performance for Everton, when <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/06/everton-coventry-premier-league-match-report">a double against Coventry</a> took the striker to 10 goals for the season in all competitions and his team temporarily up to fifth. It was high praise indeed from a manager who does not dispense tributes freely, and can appear to be on the French forward’s case constantly, but was no more than Barry deserved for a display that also featured an assist for Everton’s third goal of the night. His six Premier League goals leave him joint third alongside Evanilson of Bournemouth and Aston Villa’s Nicolas Jackson.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/thierno-barry-rise-david-moyes-purring-everton">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/wsl-talking-points-tottenham-london-city-lionesses-chelsea-arsenal</link>
      <description><p>We may have a proper title race on our hands as City and Chelsea drop points and LCL strengthen their grip on third place</p><p>Drew Spence rolled back the years with a vintage performance as her Tottenham side produced a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/manchester-city-tottenham-wsl-match-report">shock 3-1 victory</a> away against the defending champions, Manchester City. The 34-year-old marshalled the midfield and then had the vision to thread an outstanding through ball that split the City defence and found the run of Matilda Vinberg, who put Spurs 2-1 up. “She’s unbelievable. There are so many more gears in Drew and I wish I’d been able to work with her a bit earlier [in my career] because her leadership is second to none,” the Tottenham head coach, Martin Ho, said of the club captain. “Her performance levels, since I’ve been here, week on week have grown. She is covering every blade of grass and leads by example. For me, she’s one of the best midfielders in the league.” <strong>Tom Garry</strong></p><p><em><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/manchester-city-tottenham-wsl-match-report">Match report: Manchester City 1-3 Tottenham</a></em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/wsl-talking-points-tottenham-london-city-lionesses-chelsea-arsenal">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Leeds offer Chelsea a lesson, Newcastle’s summer recruits struggle and Jules Ahoka makes a name for himself</p><p>What to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. If not, United are heading only one way: down. <strong>Jamie Jackson</strong></p><p>Match report: <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report">Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United</a></p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/mauricio-pochettino-manchester-united-reign-begins-with-anfield-humiliation-liverpool">‘It’s painful for me’: Pochettino criticises Yoro red card decision</a></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/premier-league-10-talking-points-from-the-weekends-action">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Coventry edge thriller to keep Crystal Palace bottom and ruin Thomas Frank’s start</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/coventry-crystal-palace-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>New manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But sometimes the rot is so deep-rooted <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/thomas-frank-crystal-palace-premier-league">that the new manager</a> bounce manifests as nothing more than it not looking quite as shambolic as it did before. Thomas Frank started with a defeat that means Palace remain bottom of the table having lost five league games in a row.</p><p>Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. “We came through with spirit,” Lampard said. “There was good play and a big impact from the subs. It’s a good sign for the squad.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/coventry-crystal-palace-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/cesar-azpilicueta-at-chelsea-a-draw-was-a-catastrophe-if-you-cant-perform-youre-out</link>
      <description><p>Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement</p><p>César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like <em>not</em> being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot.</p><p>It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/cesar-azpilicueta-at-chelsea-a-draw-was-a-catastrophe-if-you-cant-perform-youre-out">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/20/dele-alli-tottenham-mk-dons-england</link>
      <description><p>The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player</p><p>Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality.</p><p>He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor &amp; Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/20/dele-alli-tottenham-mk-dons-england">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><ul><li><p>Keeper close to tears at Newcastle after hurting shoulder</p></li><li><p>Arsenal held 2-2, with Jaissle hailing ‘excellent’ display</p></li></ul><p>Arsenal were left sweating on the fitness of their goalkeeper David Raya after the Spaniard was forced off with a shoulder injury during the second half of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/newcastle-arsenal-premier-league-match-report">the 2-2 draw at Newcastle</a> on Saturday evening.</p><p>It left Mikel Arteta’s side six points clear of Brighton and Manchester City at the top of the Premier League but Arsenal’s manager was more concerned about Raya following an accidental collision with Newcastle’s William Osula.       <title>‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/chelsea-leeds-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p></p><p>Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.</p><p>It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/chelsea-leeds-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>Aston Villa held at home as dogged Sunderland battle for Régis Le Bris</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/aston-villa-sunderland-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>For <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/aston-villa">Aston Villa</a>, a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was another triumph of sorts. The raw numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the visitors’ box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the sole survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic seven months ago.</p><p>Villa were too predictable, short of a spark, someone to unpick an organised back line. Johan Manzambi, Emi Buendía and Alysson all flattered to deceive on an afternoon when Ibrahim Mbaye and McGinn arrived from the bench. Alejandro Garnacho, however, was not involved in Villa’s matchday squad for the second successive match and the Chelsea loanee has played just 38 minutes in the Premier League this campaign. Tammy Abraham, the match-winner in April, was also left out and a January move looks likely.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/aston-villa-sunderland-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

The latest information, news and events in France, Europe and around the world.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:50:11 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>Major cyberattack hits IT systems at Guadeloupe university hospital</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261123-major-cyberattack-hits-it-systems-at-guadeloupe-university-hospital</link><description>
A major cyberattack has disrupted the university hospital in the French overseas department of Guadeloupe, affecting its operations and forcing it to activate its emergency response plan and postponing non-emergency procedures.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0516acf0-2372-11ec-81e8-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_9M94VC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0516acf0-2372-11ec-81e8-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_9M94VC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">dee6caee-e728-11f1-80df-9f0d9c8f7db3</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:45:02 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0516acf0-2372-11ec-81e8-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_9M94VC.jpg">© Carla Bernhardt/AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French right backs Macron's plan to put public spending limits in Constitution</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261122-french-right-backs-macron-s-plan-to-put-public-spending-limits-in-constitution</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron is reportedly considering a constitutional reform to curb public deficits, with right-wing parties and the far-right National Rally signalling their willingness to support the move. The proposal could bring MPs and senators together for a vote as early as January, just months before the 2027 presidential election.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4bea9e76-e66c-11f1-b8f3-f96315fbf1b4</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 18:09:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg">AFP - STEPHANIE LECOCQ</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Students and unions unite for sixth weekend of protests across France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-students-and-unions-unite-for-sixth-weekend-of-protests-across-france</link><description>
Thousands of demonstrators took to the streets across France on Saturday for a sixth consecutive weekend of protests against rising living costs, deteriorating public services and growing inequality. The movement, which began with student demonstrations in September, has since broadened into a nationwide campaign and inspired similar rallies elsewhere in Europe.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7ad79414-e5c2-11f1-8bc6-7d93519529c2</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:43:57 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg">AFP - GUILLAUME SALIGOT</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French court finds racism played role in police beating of black music producer</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-french-court-finds-racism-played-role-in-police-beating-of-black-music-producer</link><description>
A French court has handed down prison sentences to three police officers for the violent assault of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020, ruling that racism was an aggravating factor in a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police brutality and racial discrimination.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eadc87ac-e58a-11f1-b7fe-efd3e07e368d</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:41:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg">REUTERS - Benoit Tessier</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>National Assembly backs greater legal protection for police using firearms</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-national-assembly-backs-greater-legal-protection-for-police-using-firearms</link><description>
France's parliament has approved legislation giving police officers greater legal protection when using their firearms, prompting fierce criticism from rights groups who warn it could make it harder to investigate alleged police brutality. The government insists the measure is needed to protect officers carrying out increasingly demanding duties.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a15be40c-e589-11f1-9ce2-a7af964aafae</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:44:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Nicolas Economou</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Former PM de Villepin launches 2027 presidential bid with warning to far right</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-former-pm-de-villepin-launches-20207-presidential-bid-with-warning-to-far-right</link><description>
Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin has announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election, promising to restore France's international influence, tackle growing inequality and challenge the rise of the far right. The veteran conservative also delivered a blistering assessment of President Emmanuel Macron's leadership, accusing him of allowing the country's political and social divisions to deepen.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bedb7fd4-e4ed-11f1-9e70-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324386665816.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bedb7fd4-e4ed-11f1-9e70-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324386665816.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf6f11fc-e589-11f1-b2ac-0d673b4c7b00</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 12:02:37 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bedb7fd4-e4ed-11f1-9e70-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324386665816.jpg">AP Photo/Aurelien Morissard - Aurelien Morissard</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France must change or 'risk losing' overseas territories, former PM tells RFI</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-france-must-change-or-risk-losing-overseas-territories-former-pm-tells-rfi-manuel-valls</link><description>
France's territories outside Europe are a major strategic asset, giving it a foothold on five continents and in three oceans. Yet Paris has long been accused of neglecting the nearly 3 million people living outside mainland France, who face deep economic and social inequalities. With calls for independence growing, former prime minister Manuel Valls warns that France risks losing its overseas territories unless it radically changes its relationship with them.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b00a846-f5b5-11ef-a324-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_36YE3UC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b00a846-f5b5-11ef-a324-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_36YE3UC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c2eb5f78-e343-11f1-ac1e-392da9561c55</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:31:24 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b00a846-f5b5-11ef-a324-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_36YE3UC.jpg">© AFP - DELPHINE MAYEUR </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French Greens candidate gives hard-left Mélenchon a boost in presidential race</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-french-greens-candidate-gives-hard-left-melenchon-a-boost-in-presidential-race</link><description>
French hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon has said an alliance with the Greens "should be possible", after the head of the Greens tentatively agreed to back him, angering moderates on the centre-left.

La police de l'immigration américaine est "complètement et totalement hors de contrôle", a estimé samedi le gouverneur démocrate de l'État de Washington, après l'arrestation de deux personnes dans l'aéroport international de Seattle. Des images vidéo abondamment diffusées sur les réseaux sociaux montrent deux personnes interpellées par des hommes masqués à la passerelle d'embarquement d'un avion.

Est-il encore possible d'exprimer une pensée critique en Turquie ? Le pays est-il devenu une dictature silencieuse ? Alors que le président Recep Tayyip Erdogan est omniprésent, quel champ d'action est-il possible pour l'opposition ? Turquie, une dictature silencieuse ? 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/85bc7afe-e72d-11f1-bd0e-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-6e4d78bb.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/85bc7afe-e72d-11f1-bd0e-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-6e4d78bb.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b3a23b24-e72e-11f1-9d52-43d71e86eadc</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:42:59 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Aude LECHRIST</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>États-Unis : l'ICE à nouveau critiquée après une arrestation musclée dans un aéroport</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261123-%C3%A9tats-unis-l-ice-%C3%A0-nouveau-critiqu%C3%A9e-apr%C3%A8s-une-arrestation-muscl%C3%A9e-dans-un-a%C3%A9roport</link><description>
La police de l'immigration américaine (ICE) est "complètement et totalement hors de contrôle", a estimé samedi le gouverneur démocrate de l'État de Washington (ouest), après l'arrestation de deux personnes dans un aéroport de cet État, près de Seattle. "Comme beaucoup d'Américains, je suis outré de voir des agents masqués, qui ne s'identifient pas, tirer des personnes hors des passerelles alors qu'elles embarquent sur un vol", a écrit Bob Ferguson sur X. Des images vidéo abondamment diffusées sur les réseaux sociaux samedi montrent deux personnes interpellées par des hommes masqués à la passerelle d'embarquement d'un avion.

En RD Congo, se dirige-t-on vers un report des élections générales ? Les scrutins sont prévus en décembre 2028. Dans un rapport publié en novembre, la Symocel, l’une des missions d’observation électorale, doute de la possibilité de tenir ce délai...
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0ff2bb70-e724-11f1-af33-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-d5a0039b.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0ff2bb70-e724-11f1-af33-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-d5a0039b.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">af117e7e-e6bd-11f1-b884-73184c4a7611</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 21:42:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Kalidou SY</dc:creator></item><item><category>Afrique</category><title>Libye : deux navires attaqués par des drones maritimes, dont un bateau russe</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/afrique/20261122-libye-drones-maritimes-attaqu%C3%A9-deux-navires-bateau-russe-guerre</link><description>
Un incendie s'est déclaré dimanche après une explosion à bord d'un navire russe dans la base navale de Benghazi, en Libye. Le ministère de la Santé des autorités de l'Est a indiqué que le bateau avait été "ciblé par des drones maritimes". Dans la soirée, un deuxième bateau, dont le pavillon n'a pas été communiqué, a été attaqué dans le même port. La mission de l'ONU en Libye réclame une enquête indépendante.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/659e3cc8-e6a9-11f1-ae55-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26326649718247.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/659e3cc8-e6a9-11f1-ae55-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26326649718247.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8156d5f6-e6b8-11f1-a6fb-6fc2f3d2d784</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 21:05:53 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/659e3cc8-e6a9-11f1-ae55-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26326649718247.jpg">© AP via Vanto satellite image</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Au cœur de l’info, l’invité</category><title>Rohingya : l'arrêt de la CIJ, "un des moments-clés qui changent l'Histoire"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/au-c%C5%93ur-de-l-info-l-invit%C3%A9/20261122-philippe-sands-l-arr%C3%AAt-de-la-cij-fait-partie-des-moments-cl%C3%A9s-qui-changent-l-histoire</link><description>
La Cour internationale de justice a reconnu un génocide commis par la Birmanie à l'encontre de la minorité musulmane des Rohingya. La CIJ demande à ce que les réfugiés rohingyas, pour la plupart entassés dans des camps au Bangladesh, puissent revenir en Birmanie et être indemnisés. L'avocat franco-britannique Philippe Sands, l'un des avocats qui ont représenté la Gambie contre la Birmanie devant la CIJ, était l'Invité d'Au cœur de l'info. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/224f14cc-e6b0-11f1-8ccf-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-204153-205702-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/224f14cc-e6b0-11f1-8ccf-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-204153-205702-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a96fd46c-e6b7-11f1-93d6-fb174a76721d</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 20:59:51 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Achren VERDIAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>Au cœur de l’info, l’invité</category><title>Caroline Toby : "Sans vidéosurveillance, Michel Zecler aurait été victime d'une erreur judiciaire"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/au-c%C5%93ur-de-l-info-l-invit%C3%A9/20261122-caroline-toby-sans-vid%C3%A9osurveillance-michel-zecler-aurait-%C3%A9t%C3%A9-victime-d-une-erreur-judiciaire</link><description>
Le producteur Michel Zecler avait été passé à tabac en 2020 par trois policiers dans l'entrée de son studio d'enregistrement à Paris. Les policiers avaient établi un faux procès-verbal l'accusant de violences, or les images de vidéosurveillance avaient invalidé leur version. Les policiers viennent d'être condamnés à de la prison ferme, avec interdiction d'exercer leur métier. Le caractère raciste de ces violences a aussi été reconnu. Interview de Caroline Toby, avocate de Michel Zecler.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/912ca82c-e6ac-11f1-a33d-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-201335-202201-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/912ca82c-e6ac-11f1-a33d-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-201335-202201-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">88d84f80-e6b3-11f1-a209-c955afc4fa26</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 20:30:18 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Achren VERDIAN</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>fr</language><title>France : News et actualité en continu - France 24</title><description>France 24  couvre les évènements en France et en Outre-mer : politique, culture, faits de société, énergie, crise sociale, sport, santé, avec ses reportages, enquêtes, débats et analyses.</description><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:28:50 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/fr/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>"On n'est pas dans GTA VI" : Geffray fustige une flambée de violence dans certains lycées</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261123-on-n-est-pas-gta-vi-geffray-fustige-flamb%C3%A9e-violence-lyc%C3%A9es</link><description>
Le ministre de l'Éducation nationale Édouard Geffray a fait état lundi de "98 élèves" et "une trentaine de professionnels" blessés la semaine dernière, fustigeant une recrudescence de violences, très localisées. "On n'a jamais eu autant d'élèves blessés, alors qu' (...) il n'y a jamais eu aussi peu de lycées bloqués", a-t-il pointé, appelant à une prise de conscience collective.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7fe96110-e71d-11f1-9b5b-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7QM9UJ.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7fe96110-e71d-11f1-9b5b-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7QM9UJ.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">39f94456-e720-11f1-942b-5f803ab09281</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:55:48 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7fe96110-e71d-11f1-9b5b-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7QM9UJ.jpg">© Sébastien Bozon, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Au cœur de l’info, l’invité</category><title>Caroline Toby : "Sans vidéosurveillance, Michel Zecler aurait été victime d'une erreur judiciaire"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/au-c%C5%93ur-de-l-info-l-invit%C3%A9/20261122-caroline-toby-sans-vid%C3%A9osurveillance-michel-zecler-aurait-%C3%A9t%C3%A9-victime-d-une-erreur-judiciaire</link><description>
Le producteur Michel Zecler avait été passé à tabac en 2020 par trois policiers dans l'entrée de son studio d'enregistrement à Paris. Les policiers avaient établi un faux procès-verbal l'accusant de violences, or les images de vidéosurveillance avaient invalidé leur version. Les policiers viennent d'être condamnés à de la prison ferme, avec interdiction d'exercer leur métier. Le caractère raciste de ces violences a aussi été reconnu. Interview de Caroline Toby, avocate de Michel Zecler.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/912ca82c-e6ac-11f1-a33d-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-201335-202201-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/912ca82c-e6ac-11f1-a33d-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-201335-202201-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">88d84f80-e6b3-11f1-a209-c955afc4fa26</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 20:30:18 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Achren VERDIAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Choose France : les entreprises françaises prêtes à investir 42,5 milliards d'euros</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261122-choose-france-entreprises-fran%C3%A7aises-pr%C3%AAtent-investir-42-5-milliards-euros-emmanuel-macron-%C3%A9conomie-investissements-projet</link><description>
Les entreprises tricolores projettent d'investir 42,5 milliards d'euros en France lors du sommet Choose France qui se déroulera lundi, a détaillé l'Élysée dimanche soir. Malgré une situation économique compliquée dans le pays, plus de 200 projets industriels français seront mis à l'honneur.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0b2fc994-e6ab-11f1-9ffc-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26152618587040.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0b2fc994-e6ab-11f1-9ffc-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26152618587040.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">19c1b856-e6af-11f1-a7d0-d531a8636e90</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 19:58:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0b2fc994-e6ab-11f1-9ffc-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26152618587040.jpg">© Gonzalo Fuentes, Pool Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Budget : Macron confirme qu'il envisage d'inscrire une "règle d'or" dans la Constitution</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261122-budget-macron-confirme-qu-il-envisage-d-inscrire-une-r%C3%A8gle-d-or-dans-la-constitution</link><description>
Emmanuel Macron a confirmé au Figaro qu'il envisageait de faire inscrire dans la Constitution une "règle d'or" budgétaire. Un projet qui lui permettrait de quitter l'Élysée sur une mesure emblématique, rassurante pour les marchés, alors que le président est très critiqué pour sa gestion des finances publiques.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/68d14446-e512-11f1-9a4d-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2ff1671046ae8d7a3a4d622f0cfc02f630e7ae1c.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/68d14446-e512-11f1-9a4d-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2ff1671046ae8d7a3a4d622f0cfc02f630e7ae1c.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">fea875f4-e68c-11f1-a08c-6963c92ef58d</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 15:54:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/68d14446-e512-11f1-9a4d-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2ff1671046ae8d7a3a4d622f0cfc02f630e7ae1c.jpg">© Aurelien Morissard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Suspicion de fuites vers le RN : un mail jette des soupçons sur l'implication du préfet Moutouh</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261122-fuites-au-minist%C3%A8re-de-l-int%C3%A9rieur-un-mail-jette-des-soup%C3%A7ons-sur-l-implication-du-pr%C3%A9fet-moutouh</link><description>
La justice française soupçonne des fuites d'informations confidentielles du ministère de l'Intérieur vers le Rassemblement national. Un mail pourrait apporter des éléments sur le rôle de l'ancien secrétaire général de Beauvau et actuel préfet du Loiret et de la région Centre-Val de Loire, Hugues Moutouh, qui nie toute implication.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/83540fda-e696-11f1-ba48-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324374289119.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/83540fda-e696-11f1-ba48-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324374289119.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">fb9ec900-e680-11f1-8380-d59eaff5322f</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 14:28:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/83540fda-e696-11f1-ba48-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324374289119.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, Pool AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Présidentielle 2027 : François Ruffin jette l'éponge face à "l’impasse" de sa campagne</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261121-pr%C3%A9sidentielle-prenant-acte-de-l-impasse-de-sa-campagne-fran%C3%A7ois-ruffin-retire-sa-candidature</link><description>
À cinq mois de l’échéance, François Ruffin a annoncé, samedi, qu’il retirait sa candidature à l’élection présidentielle, prenant "acte de l’impasse" de sa campagne faute d’avoir réussi à imposer l’organisation d’une "grande primaire" de toute la gauche.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/049bdf84-e5d2-11f1-b9d8-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6J962D.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/049bdf84-e5d2-11f1-b9d8-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6J962D.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">34a0106a-e5d2-11f1-88ab-0f8d44227e2e</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 17:37:20 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/049bdf84-e5d2-11f1-b9d8-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6J962D.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Syndicats, jeunesse et gilets jaunes un peu moins mobilisés pour le sixième samedi de manifestation</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261121-en-direct-acte-vi-de-la-mobilisation-pour-la-jeunesse-et-contre-la-vie-ch%C3%A8re</link><description>
Pour la sixième semaine consécutive, syndicats, organisations de jeunesse et Gilets jaunes ont manifesté contre la vie chère, dans un contexte de colère sociale devenue européenne mais qui commence à s'essouffler en France. Le ministère de l'Intérieur a dénombré au total 82 500 manifestants dans l'Hexagone, dont 21 500 à Paris. La CGT parle de son côté de 150 000 manifestants dans le pays, 45 000 dans la capitale.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d69a9eb2-e5cd-11f1-820c-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88L88H.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d69a9eb2-e5cd-11f1-820c-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88L88H.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e164d32e-e584-11f1-8432-8fa90dee50f1</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:23:49 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d69a9eb2-e5cd-11f1-820c-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88L88H.jpg">AFP - GUILLAUME SALIGOT</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Entre 80 000 et 150 000 personnes mobilisées pour un sixième samedi de manifestations en France</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261121-sixi%C3%A8me-samedi-de-manifestation-contre-la-vie-ch%C3%A8re-premier-round-contre-les-violences-sexistes</link><description>
Pour la sixième semaine d'affilée, des syndicats, organisations de jeunesse et Gilets jaunes ont appelé à manifester, samedi, contre la vie chère. Malgré une baisse de la mobilisation, 82 500 personnes ont défilé en France selon le ministère de l’intérieur et 150 000 selon les organisateurs.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0daede70-e445-11f1-aa9e-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/6eafad5bb555456f4505bd99516b8a173e5764e7.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0daede70-e445-11f1-aa9e-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/6eafad5bb555456f4505bd99516b8a173e5764e7.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">844245cc-e52b-11f1-ab61-a5c9daa303ca</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 21:54:13 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0daede70-e445-11f1-aa9e-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/6eafad5bb555456f4505bd99516b8a173e5764e7.jpg">© Benoit PEYRUCQ / AFP/Archives</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Au cœur de l’info, l’invité</category><title>Johann Chapoutot : "la dédiabolisation du RN est véritablement un mythe"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/au-c%C5%93ur-de-l-info-l-invit%C3%A9/20261120-johann-chapoutot-la-d%C3%A9diabolisation-du-rn-est-v%C3%A9ritablement-un-mythe</link><description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/84d2817a-e524-11f1-9187-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C8TV3VK.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/84d2817a-e524-11f1-9187-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C8TV3VK.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ec88460c-e514-11f1-8bce-43bc8e8d3f8d</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 19:02:24 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/84d2817a-e524-11f1-9187-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C8TV3VK.jpg">© Geoffroy van der Hasselt, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Fuites au ministère de l'Intérieur : comment le RN a progressivement séduit les hauts fonctionnaires</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261120-fuites-au-minist%C3%A8re-de-l-int%C3%A9rieur-comment-le-rn-a-progressivement-s%C3%A9duit-les-hauts-fonctionnaires</link><description>
Le parquet de Paris soupçonne l'ancien secrétaire général de Beauvau et actuel préfet du Loiret et de la région Centre-Val de Loire, Hugues Moutouh, d'avoir informé le Rassemblement national sur des enquêtes judiciaires visant le parti. </description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ed281fb0-e4ec-11f1-b121-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ed281fb0-e4ec-11f1-b121-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">845e625a-e4fb-11f1-8ece-9d792c6a9305</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:12:25 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ed281fb0-e4ec-11f1-b121-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg">© Pascal Guyot, AFP</source><dc:creator>Louis CHAHUNEAU</dc:creator></item><item><category>Outre-Mer</category><title>De l'océan Indien aux Caraïbes, la sécheresse frappe plusieurs territoires d'Outre-mer</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/outre-mer/20261120-de-l-oc%C3%A9an-indien-aux-cara%C3%AFbes-la-s%C3%A9cheresse-frappe-plusieurs-territoires-d-outre-mer</link><description>
La sécheresse s'installe durablement en Outre-mer. Le manque d'eau fragilise les cultures et menace les récoltes aux Antilles et à La Réunion. La situation est également très préoccupante en Guyane, où le niveau du fleuve continue de baisser.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d5ba9aa2-e4f5-11f1-a177-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-e00d5d0f.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d5ba9aa2-e4f5-11f1-a177-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-e00d5d0f.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">668bbe98-e4ca-11f1-b006-117a06c45e07</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:36:16 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator></dc:creator></item><item><category>ActuElles</category><title>Les féminicides, la partie émergée du contrôle coercitif</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/actuelles/20261120-les-f%C3%A9minicides-la-partie-%C3%A9merg%C3%A9e-du-contr%C3%B4le-coercitif</link><description>
Les féminicides font aussi des victimes invisibles : les proches des femmes assassinées, confrontées à un deuil impossible et à des embûches judiciaires. Dans 75 % des cas, le féminicide survient sans violences physiques préalables, mais au terme d'une période de contrôle coercitif :  une prison invisible faite d'emprise et de violences psychologiques, explique l'historienne Christelle Taraud, qui décrit des victimes "zombifiées" par leur tortionnaire.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/804fd37e-e4e7-11f1-94db-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/actuelles-4.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/804fd37e-e4e7-11f1-94db-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/actuelles-4.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">012b0ea0-e4e8-11f1-954f-b12e286687bf</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:46:33 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Laure MANENT</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Gérard Depardieu et Michel Houellebecq accusés de viol en réunion et d'agressions sexuelles</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261120-g%C3%A9rard-depardieu-et-michel-houellebecq-accus%C3%A9s-de-viol-en-r%C3%A9union-et-d-agressions-sexuelles</link><description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0daede70-e445-11f1-aa9e-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/6eafad5bb555456f4505bd99516b8a173e5764e7.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0daede70-e445-11f1-aa9e-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/6eafad5bb555456f4505bd99516b8a173e5764e7.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0e8098a2-e445-11f1-9e16-9f17a13d179f</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 18:14:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0daede70-e445-11f1-aa9e-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/6eafad5bb555456f4505bd99516b8a173e5764e7.jpg">© Benoit Peyrucq, AFP/Archives</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Présidentielle : les créateurs de contenus sommés de respecter le pluralisme par l'Arcom</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261119-pr%C3%A9sidentielle-cr%C3%A9ateurs-contenus-somm%C3%A9s-respecter-pluralisme-arcom</link><description>
Créateurs de contenus et influenceurs devront pour la première fois respecter les règles du pluralisme pendant la campagne de la présidentielle 2027, au même titre que la radio et la télévision, a annoncé jeudi le régulateur de l'audiovisuel et du numérique. En cas de manquements répétés, l'Arcom pourra décider de sanctions financières. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1246ec08-e430-11f1-b9da-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32687U6.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1246ec08-e430-11f1-b9da-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32687U6.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8d488a52-e42f-11f1-aa64-9157722348a5</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 18:07:37 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1246ec08-e430-11f1-b9da-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32687U6.jpg">© Joël Saget, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Le RN visé par une nouvelle enquête autour de fuites impliquant un préfet</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261119-le-rn-vis%C3%A9-par-une-nouvelle-enqu%C3%AAte-autour-de-fuites-impliquant-un-pr%C3%A9fet</link><description>
À quelques mois de la présidentielle, le siège du Rassemblement national, ainsi que le ministère de l'Intérieur, ont été perquisitionnés par des juges d'instruction dans le cadre d'une nouvelle affaire judiciaire liée à des soupçons de fuites d'informations vers le RN, impliquant un préfet.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0cecf33c-e445-11f1-91e4-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/ec3a5b7b2f106b3dc8864450a3619a771fda0000.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0cecf33c-e445-11f1-91e4-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/ec3a5b7b2f106b3dc8864450a3619a771fda0000.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4c941b6e-e440-11f1-92f2-af61307a37ad</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 17:40:23 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0cecf33c-e445-11f1-91e4-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/ec3a5b7b2f106b3dc8864450a3619a771fda0000.jpg">© Alain Jocard, AFP/Archives</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Les clés de l'info</category><title>"Femmeblancherie" : le procès de la haine des femmes</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/les-cl%C3%A9s-de-l-info/20261118-femmeblancherie-le-proc%C3%A8s-de-la-haine-des-femmes</link><description>
Ce mercredi s’est ouvert le procès de sept membres du canal Telegram "Femmeblancherie" au tribunal judiciaire de Paris. Appels aux féminicides et aux viols, fichages racistes et homophobes, plusieurs dizaines d’abonnés sont accusés d’une trentaine de crimes et délits, dont "provocation publique à commettre un crime". Un procès qui découle d’une idéologie très en vogue chez les jeunes, notamment sur les réseaux sociaux : le masculinisme.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3a6bb852-e3a5-11f1-b778-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/FRAN261118-2339-Live-CS2339.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3a6bb852-e3a5-11f1-b778-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/FRAN261118-2339-Live-CS2339.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">53cba342-e3a6-11f1-92ea-c561305b4ba1</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 23:18:12 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Cécile GALLUCCIO</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>
